sample.name: Benjamin Cooper House
facts: Being remade into an American Revolution museum.
Address: 60 Erie Street, Camden

sample.name: Alpha Pi Lambda
facts: Built by Dilks for Philadelphia brewer Frederick Poth in 1887.
Contains 16 bedrooms.
Home of the Drexel University chapter of the Alpha Pi Lambda fraternity.

sample.name: Kensington High School
facts: About 36 m (118 ft) tall
Address: 2075 East Cumberland Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: George W. Childs Elementary School
facts: About 29 m (96 ft) tall
Address: 1235 South 16th Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Historical Price sawmill dam?
facts: Joseph Price built a saw mill on Indian Creek, in what is now Shortridge Park.

sample.name: Glen Fern
facts: Also called the Livezey House; built around 1725 by Thomas Shoemaker.
Sold in 1747 to Thomas Livezey Jr., who built a mill on the site.
Livezey descendants lived there for more than 120 years.

sample.name: Sweetbriar Mansion
facts: Federal style mansion built in 1797 in West Fairmount Park by Samuel Breck.
Named for the roses that grew on the property.
Became part of the park in 1869 and is headquarters of the Modern Club of Philadelphia.

sample.name: Edwin Forrest House
facts: Built in 1853 to 1854 for brewer William Gaul, designed by architect Stephen D. Button in the Italianate style.
Actor Edwin Forrest bought it a year after completion and lived there until his death in 1872.
Housed the Philadelphia School of Design for Women from 1880 until 1960.

sample.name: Monastery Mansion
facts: Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places
Also known as The Monastery
About 14 m (45 ft) tall

sample.name: Narberth War Memorial
facts: Installed on May 15, 1926 in front of the Narberth Community Building.
Moved to its present site on May 31, 1937.
Installed by Harold D. Speakman Post 356 of the American Legion.

sample.name: 1st Regiment Infantry National Guard of Philadelphia
facts: Bronze statue by the American sculptor Henry Kirke Bush-Brown.
Founded in 1911
Also known as Spirit of ’61

sample.name: George W. Nebinger School
facts: Designed by Irwin T. Catharine and built in 1924 to 1925 in the Art Deco style.
Four-story, nine-bay brick building on a raised basement.
Entrance portico has Doric columns, with a brick parapet at the roofline.

sample.name: Philadelphia Korean War Memorial
facts: Dedicated June 22, 2002 and rededicated on May 28, 2007.
Commemorates 610 servicemen from the Philadelphia area who died in the Korean War.
Features four black granite pillars listing casualties from each year of the war, 1950 to 1953.

sample.name: Joey Giardello Statue
facts: Bronze statue by sculptor Carl LeVotch, installed on a triangle at Passyunk Avenue and 13th Street.
Unveiled on May 21, 2011, honoring the 1963 world middleweight champion.

sample.name: Expedition Escape
facts: Escape room venue with private adventures for groups of 2 to 68 players.
Games include Lucky Dice Diner, set in a 1950s diner, and The Blind Tiger Speakeasy, set in 1920s Prohibition.
Address: 601 South Henderson Road

sample.name: Sedgley Porter House
facts: Stone porter's house designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe, built around 1799 to 1802.
Latrobe's only surviving building in Philadelphia; the main Sedgeley mansion was demolished.
Served as a park guard house and jail for over a century before conversion to offices.

sample.name: Edwin M. Stanton School
facts: Designed by Irwin T. Catharine and built in 1925 to 1926 in the Art Deco style.
Entrance has a portico with Doric columns and terra cotta colored tiles.
Named for Edwin M. Stanton, who was Secretary of War under Abraham Lincoln.

sample.name: Harbison's Dairy Milk Bottle
facts: The 30,000-gallon tank is built to look like a glass milk bottle.
Part of the Harbisons' Dairies complex; main building dates to 1895.
Added to the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places in 2018.

sample.name: Gloria Dei Church
facts: Founded in 1698
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places
Also known as Old Swedes' Church

sample.name: All Wars Memorial to Colored Soldiers and Sailors
facts: Sculpted by Philadelphia artist J. Otto Schweizer.
Stood hidden behind Memorial Hall in West Fairmount Park until moved to the Parkway in 1994.
Proposed by legislator Samuel Beecher Hart, with state funds appropriated in 1927.

sample.name: Angel of the Resurrection
facts: Depicts an angel lifting a fallen soldier from flames.
Part of a monument to 1,307 Pennsylvania Railroad workers who died in World War II.
Founded in 1952

sample.name: Monument to Six Million Jewish Martyrs
facts: Sculpted by Nathan Rapoport.
Dates from 1964
Inscription: “NOW AND FOREVER ENSHRINED IN MEMORY ARE THE SIX MILLION JEWISH MARTYRS WHO PERISHED IN CONCENTRATION CAMPS GHETTOS AND GAS CHAMBERS.”

sample.name: Old Federal Reserve Bank Building
facts: 7 stories tall
Address: 925 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Merion Tribute House
facts: Funded by Eldridge Johnson, founder of the Victor Talking Machine Company, to honor 81 Merion men in service.
Designed by architects Karcher and Smith in Gothic patterns with local stone.
Ironwork and lamps were designed by craftsmen of Samuel Yellin.

sample.name: Boelson Cottage
facts: Also known as John Boelsen House
About 6 m (21 ft) tall
Address: 2128 Martin Luther King Drive, Philadelphia
